narrative:
The model estimates a 64% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors that, in combination, signal a higher risk of departure compared to colleagues who are expected to stay.

The strongest influence is that you have received other job opportunities while at your current company. Most employees predicted to stay (77%) report receiving no such offers, so this stands out as a clear pull toward leaving. Next, your difficult work-life balance also pushes the prediction toward departure. While only 9% of stayers report a difficult balance, this challenge appears to be weighing on your decision to remain. Finally, having 6-10 years of total professional experience contributes to the prediction of leaving. This is somewhat surprising, as half of those expected to stay have fewer years (1-5), but in your specific combination of circumstances, your mid-career experience level slightly increases the model's estimated likelihood of moving on.

Taken together, these elements outweigh many positive aspects of your profile, such as high emotional commitment, strong job support, and overall job satisfaction. The organization should discuss ways to improve your work-life balance and explore whether internal opportunities can match what external offers provide. You may wish to reflect on how these factors align with your long-term goals before making any decisions. (248 words)
